job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

passage: In our science lab, we observed how matter behaves under different conditions. First, we placed a crystal of potassium permanganate into a beaker of water. We watched as the purple color spread throughout the liquid without stirring, demonstrating that particles of matter are constantly moving and have spaces between them. Next, we heated a block of ice in a beaker. We noticed that even as we continued to supply heat, the thermometer reading remained steady at zero degrees Celsius until all the ice had melted. This shows that heat energy is used to overcome the forces of attraction between particles rather than increasing their kinetic energy. We then compared the evaporation of water on a dry, sunny day versus a humid, rainy day. We found that water evaporates much slower when the air is already saturated with water vapor. Finally, we used a syringe to compress air. We observed that the volume of air decreased significantly because the particles are far apart, not because the individual particles themselves change in size. These experiments prove that matter is composed of tiny, discrete particles that possess kinetic energy and occupy specific arrangements, rather than being a continuous, solid mass.

items.evidence: We watched as the purple color spread throughout the liquid without stirring, demonstrating that particles of matter are constantly moving and have spaces between them.
items.q: Potassium permanganate colours the whole beaker of water without stirring. What does this show about matter?
options: Its particles always move and have gaps between them
It is one continuous mass with no particles
Air in its gaps carries the colour around
A force pulls its purple particles close together
items.explain: The colour spreads on its own because particles keep moving and have spaces between them.

wrong.why: thinks matter is a continuous block
thinks the gaps between particles are filled with air
thinks diffusion is a force pulling particles together

items.evidence: This shows that heat energy is used to overcome the forces of attraction between particles rather than increasing their kinetic energy.
items.q: Ice keeps getting heat while melting, yet its temperature does not rise. Why?
options: Heat breaks the attraction holding particles together
Heat makes the particles move faster and faster
Heat makes each particle grow bigger in size
Heat escapes because ice particles cannot move
items.explain: During melting, heat is used to overcome attraction between particles, not to raise their kinetic energy.

wrong.why: thinks added heat always raises temperature and particle speed
thinks particles in a solid do not move

items.evidence: We found that water evaporates much slower when the air is already saturated with water vapor.
items.q: Meena hangs wet clothes out on a rainy day with damp air. How will they dry?
options: They dry slower, because the air already holds vapour
They dry faster, because moist air speeds up evaporation
They dry only when the water starts to boil
They dry equally fast, because air moisture has no effect
items.explain: Water evaporates much slower when the air is already full of water vapour.

wrong.why: thinks evaporation happens only at boiling point
ignores the comparison made in the experiment

items.evidence: We observed that the volume of air decreased significantly because the particles are far apart, not because the individual particles themselves change in size.
items.q: Why can the air in a syringe be pushed into a much smaller space?
options: Its particles have large gaps between them
Its particles shrink in size when pushed
Its particles are soft and get squashed
Its gaps hold air that gets squeezed out
items.explain: Air compresses because its particles are far apart, not because the particles change size.

wrong.why: thinks gas particles are soft and squishy
thinks the space between particles is filled with air
